scope: Royal residence at Sans-Souci, Milot, in its late royal configuration. Includes the main palace and its north double staircase, fountain and immediate rear approach.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Palace was inaugurated in 1813; the main building was Henry I’s residence. The 1842 earthquake seriously damaged the structure.
Ritter’s firsthand 1820 account describes two principal storeys, the main stairs, fountain, early glazing and hilltop setting. He recorded full completion in 1817.
Mackenzie’s 1830 book Volume 2 is the original publication of the Clarke print.
Milot Archaeological Project reports surviving original main facades, neoclassical symmetry, Doric treatment and two monumental staircases.
Architectural survey describes an entrance-side fountain between monumental stairs, and a rear facade with a curved central pediment.
Heritage authority identifies the ceremonial access stair with the north facade.
